A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RULEBREAKERS study despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original accuracy, confidence, familiarity and attribution experiments on six LLMs, with additional prompt-sensitivity and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds GPT-4o evaluations, prompting and generation experiments, logic-enhanced model comparisons and neuron-activation analyses.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction procedure, entity inventories and four rulebreaker templates are retained. The added prompting variants and external logic systems are experimental conditions and comparators; no new proposed algorithm or model component is introduced.

E1.justification: The same English geographical/categorical MT/DS dataset is retained. Appendix I adds premise-only conclusion generation to supplied-conclusion judgment, extending task requirements within the existing domains and reasoning patterns.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's six LLMs, v2 evaluates GPT-4o and adds Llama-3.1-8B before/after logic fine-tuning, plus GPT-3.5-turbo with direct prompting, two-shot CoT, LogicLM and SymbolicCoT (Appendix K, Table 10). This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds factual-knowledge instructions, alternative questions and prefixed premises; conclusion generation with a 50-token limit, output parsing and sampling temperatures of 0.1, 0.5 and 1.0; and logic-system execution/fallback protocols (Appendices H–K). The original ten-phrasing evaluation remains documented.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the original sensitivity and attribution analyses with instruction/premise-framing controls, decoding sensitivity, controlled logic-enhancement comparisons and layerwise neuron-activation analysis (Appendices H, I, K and N). These test additional robustness and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: V1 already reports 95% confidence intervals, Welch tests and attribution-ratio standard deviations. V2 additionally reports standard deviations for confidence and familiarity in Tables 2–3, previously presented as plots. This expands dispersion reporting without establishing additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results for new models and experiments. Table 10 reports GPT-3.5-turbo paired accuracy of 50.80% directly, 65.36% with CoT, 30.81% with LogicLM and 9.53% with SymbolicCoT. Retained results also change: Gemma's paired accuracy changes from 0.096 to 0.071 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 4), alongside revised attribution values and rankings.

T1.justification: The principal logical rules and metric definitions remain substantively equivalent. However, v2's redrawn Figure 1 introduces an inconsistent symbolic inference: 'A or B' and 'Not B' produce 'Not A', although its text correctly gives conclusion A. V1's illustration correctly presents modus tollens.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes LLMs' failure to integrate logical reasoning and factual knowledge. V2 adds a central claim that formal-logic enhancements can increase divergence from human-like reasoning, making this trade-off prominent in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of prompting trade-offs, DS/MT structural similarity, logic enhancement and neuron activation, and revises familiarity/attention explanations around changed exceptions. It removes v1's explicit scope-limitations discussion and warning that the findings do not establish internal symbolic reasoning.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code/dataset release; v2 reports a public dataset release and supplies its repository address. V2 also documents GPT-4o's version and evaluation dates, generation/parsing procedures, comparator implementations and fallback behavior. Existing hardware, batching, runtime and license information is retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands cognitive-science grounding, including Table 5 linking templates to prior human experiments. It adds detailed comparisons with human–LLM reasoning research and Holliday et al., and develops its positioning against logic-enhancement approaches, replacing much of v1's textual-entailment framing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 incorporates worked explanations into the introduction, reorganizes retained appendix material, removes the standalone Limitations section and introduces several new appendix sections.

P2.justification: V2 changes conference formatting and appendix layout, redraws Figure 1, replaces confidence/familiarity plots with Tables 2–3, expands accuracy plots to seven models and adds comparison tables and generation/activation figures. These are substantial changes to visual organization, beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Appendices H–I test whether the original findings depend on question wording or supplied conclusions, while Appendix K directly investigates logic-enhancement trade-offs. Together with clearer cognitive-science grounding and reported dataset access, these substantially strengthen the paper's evidence and usefulness. Removing explicit limitations and introducing the Figure 1 inference error are regressions, but they do not outweigh these gains.
